tags: why does my dog know when i'm coming home
script: There's no car in the driveway yet, no keys jingling, nothing obvious has happened, and yet your dog is already sitting by the door, tail wagging, clearly expecting you any second. This isn't magic, it comes down to a combination of incredibly sharp senses and pattern recognition. Dogs can hear sounds at frequencies and distances far beyond human hearing, meaning a car that sounds identical to you from two streets away might be clearly distinguishable to your dog's ears from much farther out. Many dogs also learn to associate specific daily patterns, a certain time of day, the sound of a neighbor's routine that tends to overlap with yours, or subtle household cues, with your imminent return. Some researchers also point to scent as a factor, your smell fading from the house in a predictable pattern throughout the day may give dogs another subtle timing cue. It's a great reminder of just how tuned in dogs are to the rhythms of their household, even the ones we don't consciously notice ourselves. That eager wait by the door isn't a coincidence, it's your dog reading a pattern they've quietly mastered.
